claims.text: A refractory high-entropy alloy that forms a stable protective oxide layer under elevated-temperature wear conditions will resist tribo-corrosion better than conventional structural alloys.
The proposed material is a homogeneous HEA containing multiple principal refractory or corrosion-resistant elements.
A microstructure favorable for uniform oxidation contributes to the proposed HEA's performance.
The HEA forms a stable, adherent passivating oxide film during tribo-corrosion exposure.
The passivating oxide film mitigates mechanical wear.
The passivating oxide film inhibits further chemical attack.
Synergy among the HEA's constituent elements enables uniform oxidation.
Uniform oxidation produces a continuous protective oxide film.
The continuous oxide film reduces direct exposure of the underlying metal to corrosive agents.
The continuous oxide film reduces mechanical stress imposed on the underlying metal.
Reduced exposure to corrosive agents and mechanical stress slows degradation.
The proposed HEA will have a lower tribo-corrosion wear rate than traditional structural alloys under comparable conditions.
The proposed HEA will exhibit less mass loss than traditional structural alloys under comparable tribo-corrosion conditions.
The proposed HEA will maintain a more stable oxide film than traditional structural alloys under comparable tribo-corrosion conditions.
Traditional single- or dual-principal-element structural alloys lack a microstructure tailored for optimal protective oxide-film formation under tribo-corrosion conditions.
The proposed performance advantage depends on the protective oxide forming and remaining stable.
Temperatures or corrosive conditions beyond the oxide film's stability range may diminish the HEA's performance advantage.
